blocks.heading: Causes of conflict
blocks.text: Conflict can arise from competing objectives, scarce resources, unclear responsibilities, perceived unfairness, poor communication or disputed changes to pay and conditions. A department may seek more output while another protects quality; workers may see an unexplained rota as unfair. Identify a causal link: a vague allocation can leave two people expecting the other to finish a task, leading to blame and delay. Do not treat the resulting strike or argument as the underlying cause. Listening and information can resolve misunderstanding, while a genuine distributional dispute may still require negotiation.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Tula Stores changes weekend shifts without explaining its selection rule. Staff believe the same people receive inconvenient hours. Perceived unfairness and missing information can undermine trust and cooperation. Explain the rule, hear evidence and review the allocation rather than assuming the dispute is caused by workers disliking work.
